adjudication_changelog.resolved_value: No multiplicity correction for frequentist key secondary analyses (all p-values nominal); Bayesian analyses stated not to require multiplicity adjustment
adjudication_changelog.quote: Bayesian analyses did not require adjustment for multiplicity by nature of the Bayesian approach. Conventional analyses were performed using a mixed effects model with repeated measures (MMRM) comparing placebo to active arms. All listed p -values for key secondary endpoints using conventional statistics are nominal, and no correction was applied for multiplicity.
adjudication_changelog.reasoning: Both readings capture the same fact — no multiplicity adjustment for either analysis stream — at different levels of detail; reading A is the more precise supported version. Reading B's phrase 'none stated for Bayesian' is slightly inaccurate, since the document explicitly states that Bayesian analyses did not require adjustment rather than being silent on it.

adjudication_changelog.quote: The primary endpoint was met if the Bayesian analysis, when all subjects completed 12 months of treatment, met the threshold of an 80% probability that the ED90 dose achieved at least 25% less clinical decline compared to placebo on ADCOMS.
adjudication_changelog.reasoning: The document describes the primary endpoint only as a single prespecified Bayesian probability threshold and never states that any type I error / multiplicity control procedure was applied to it, so 'yes' is not supported; the multiplicity statements in the document are directed at the key secondary endpoints and at Bayesian analyses generally.

adjudication_changelog.disposition: advisory only — harm entries are not rewritten from a presence ruling
adjudication_changelog.quote: In this study, ARIA-H (new cerebral microhemorrhages, cerebral macrohemorrhages, and superficial siderosis) regardless of the presence of ARIA-E were observed in 13 (5.3%) subjects in the placebo group ( N = 245) compared to 65 (10.7%) subjects in the lecanemab groups ( N = 609).
adjudication_changelog.reasoning: Reading A ('reported') overstates, because only the composite ARIA-H is quantified and cerebral macrohemorrhage appears solely inside the composite's definition; reading B ('absent') also overstates, because the harm is named in the document and nowhere declared absent or zero.

adjudication_changelog.resolved_value: 64% probability of being better than placebo with 25% less decline on ADCOMS at 12 months (threshold was 80%)
adjudication_changelog.quote: The primary analysis conducted at month 12 of treatment for all subjects indicated that the 10 mg/kg biweekly (ED90) dose had a 64% probability of being better than placebo with 25% less decline on ADCOMS at 12 months, missing the pre-specified 80% probability threshold for the primary outcome (Table ). As such, the primary endpoint was not met.
adjudication_changelog.reasoning: The document prints reading B's value essentially verbatim: the primary endpoint's reported quantity is the posterior probability of 64% against the prespecified 80% threshold, corroborated by Table 2 (Pr (CSD) = 0.638 for 10 mg/kg biweekly). Reading A's null is wrong because the document does state the primary result.

adjudication_changelog.quote: The primary analysis conducted at month 12 of treatment for all subjects indicated that the 10 mg/kg biweekly (ED90) dose had a 64% probability of being better than placebo with 25% less decline on ADCOMS at 12 months, missing the pre-specified 80% probability threshold for the primary outcome (Table ). As such, the primary endpoint was not met.
adjudication_changelog.reasoning: The primary endpoint is reported only as a posterior probability against a threshold; Table 2 gives change-from-baseline means and SDs plus posterior probabilities (Pr (Max), Pr (ED90), Pr Superiority, Pr (CSD)) and no interval estimate. No confidence or credible interval for the 12-month ADCOMS primary appears anywhere in the document.

title.value: A randomized, double-blind, phase 2b proof-of-concept clinical trial in early Alzheimer’s disease with lecanemab, an anti-Aβ protofibril antibody
title.quote: A randomized, double-blind, phase 2b proof-of-concept clinical trial in early Alzheimer’s disease with lecanemab, an anti-Aβ protofibril antibody

design.value: 18-month, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled Bayesian design clinical trial employing response adaptive randomization across placebo and five lecanemab arms
design.quote: Study 201 ( NCT01767311 ) was an 18-month, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled Bayesian design clinical trial employing response adaptive randomization across placebo and five lecanemab arms (2.5 mg/kg biweekly, 5 mg/kg monthly, 5 mg/kg biweekly, 10 mg/kg monthly, 10 mg/kg biweekly)

phase.quote: a phase 2b proof-of-concept, dose-ranging efficacy study using a novel Bayesian adaptive design was initiated to assess the effects of lecanemab in subjects with mild cognitive impairment due to AD and mild AD dementia

n.quote: A total of 856 subjects were randomized and 854 were treated (lecanemab, 609; placebo, 245) between December 2012 and November 2017 at 117 sites across North America

n_description.value: 854 randomized subjects were treated (lecanemab, 609; placebo, 245); 856 subjects were randomized in total
n_description.quote: A total of 856 subjects were randomized and 854 were treated (lecanemab, 609; placebo, 245) between December 2012 and November 2017 at 117 sites across North America

population.value: Subjects with early Alzheimer's disease in 2 subgroups — mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild AD dementia — all confirmed amyloid positive by amyloid PET or CSF Aβ1–42, with objective episodic memory impairment on WMS-IV LMII and MMSE ≥22 at screening and baseline
population.quote: Participants comprised 2 subgroups: mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild AD dementia. All subjects were confirmed amyloid positive via amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) Aβ 1–42 for eligibility.

followup.quote: Understanding the importance of 18-month data in the context of AD clinical trials assessing slowing of disease progression, all randomized subjects were to complete the full 18 months of treatment.

intervention.value: Lecanemab (BAN2401) in five arms: 2.5 mg/kg biweekly, 5 mg/kg monthly, 5 mg/kg biweekly, 10 mg/kg monthly, 10 mg/kg biweekly
intervention.quote: across placebo and five lecanemab arms (2.5 mg/kg biweekly, 5 mg/kg monthly, 5 mg/kg biweekly, 10 mg/kg monthly, 10 mg/kg biweekly) to assess safety and efficacy in subjects with early Alzheimer’s disease

comparator.value: Placebo, given as biweekly infusions to maintain the blind
comparator.quote: To maintain the blind, all subjects received biweekly infusions of either placebo or lecanemab.

biomarker_confirmation.value: Amyloid positivity confirmed via amyloid PET or CSF Aβ1–42
biomarker_confirmation.quote: All subjects were confirmed amyloid positive via amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) Aβ 1–42 for eligibility.

limitations: Most notably, a small number of symptomatic ARIA-E cases at 10 mg/kg biweekly prompted one Regulatory Authority to request that subsequent ApoE4+ subjects (approximately 70% of the overall study population) not be randomized to the 10 mg/kg biweekly dose.

An additional component to the request required that all ApoE4+ subjects on 10 mg/kg biweekly who were on study but who had not yet reached 6 months of treatment be immediately discontinued ( N = 25 subjects).

Implementation of these actions led to early (initiated between 300 and 350 randomized participants) and significant changes to the study design that resulted in a marked imbalance in the number of ApoE4+ subjects on 10 mg/kg biweekly (30% ApoE4+ subjects).
The constraints in this analysis were specifically associated with the ED90 dose and therefore could have had an impact on the ability to interpret the results.
Data between the mild AD dementia and the MCI subgroups within the study population were generally consistent but limited and difficult to interpret due to small sample size
There was no sample size analysis for the CSF substudy and results for biomarker analyses are presented descriptively.
The 10 mg/kg biweekly group, despite being limited in size and ApoE4+ balance, showed nominally significant differences versus placebo on ADCOMS and ADAS-Cog14 at 18 months of treatment.
None of the other dose groups differed from placebo most likely due to the relatively small sample size allocated to these sub-optimal doses by the Bayesian adaptive randomization algorithm.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The trial was funded by Eisai Inc., authors from Eisai had input into design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, report writing and the decision to publish, and most authors are Eisai, BioArctic or Berry Consultants employees.
risk_of_bias.quote: This trial was funded by Eisai Inc. Authors from Eisai Inc. had input into the study design; in the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data; in the writing of the report; and in the decision to submit the paper for publication.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Differential discontinuation between arms (23.7% placebo vs 36.0% lecanemab), largely driven by protocol-mandated discontinuation for ARIA-E and by the regulatory-imposed discontinuation of ApoE4 carriers on 10 mg/kg biweekly.
risk_of_bias.quote: Discontinuations occurred in 23.7% for placebo- and 36.0% for lecanemab-treated subjects.

risk_of_bias.judgement: All subjects with MRI-detected ARIA-E were discontinued immediately per protocol regardless of severity or symptoms, a treatment-related event that removed subjects from active treatment.
risk_of_bias.quote: All subjects with ARIA-E as assessed by MRI were discontinued immediately per protocol, regardless of radiologic severity or symptomatic status.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The ED90 dose group (10 mg/kg biweekly) had a markedly lower proportion of ApoE4 carriers (30%) than all other groups (71-91%) because of the mid-study regulatory randomization restriction.
risk_of_bias.quote: the lecanemab 10 mg/kg biweekly group had fewer subjects compared to 10 mg/kg monthly with a lower percentage of ApoE4 carriers (30%) relative to all other treatment groups (placebo 71%; 2.5 mg/kg biweekly 73%; 5 mg/kg monthly 77%; 5 mg/kg biweekly 91%; 10 mg/kg monthly 89%)

risk_of_bias.judgement: More male subjects in the lecanemab group relative to placebo (54% vs 42%).
risk_of_bias.quote: with the exception of more male subjects in the lecanemab group relative to placebo (54% vs 42%; Table )

risk_of_bias.judgement: All key secondary frequentist p-values are nominal with no multiplicity correction, and the document states all reported p values are nominal because the primary endpoint was not met.
risk_of_bias.quote: All reported p values are considered nominal because the primary endpoint was not met.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The randomization design was altered between 300 and 350 randomized subjects at a regulator's request, splitting the randomization probability vector by ApoE4 carrier status.
risk_of_bias.quote: However, before the interim analysis of 350 subjects, Health Authorities restricted randomization around ApoE4 carrier status, whereby ApoE4 carriers (hetero- or homozygous) were not to be randomized to the 10 mg/kg biweekly dose going forward.

disagreements.question: Does a trial whose 12-month primary endpoint was not met nevertheless establish proof of concept for lecanemab?
disagreements.position: The document concludes that proof of concept was supported by prespecified key secondary endpoint analyses despite the primary endpoint not being met.
disagreements.attributed_to: The study authors (Eisai Inc. and co-authors of this article)
disagreements.quote: Proof of concept was supported through prespecified key secondary endpoint analyses, where lecanemab treatment resulted in a dose dependent and consistent reduction in clinical decline relative to placebo across a number of clinical endpoints according to Bayesian and frequentist approaches.

disagreements.question: Was the Regulatory Authority's restriction of the 10 mg/kg biweekly dose in ApoE4 carriers appropriate?
disagreements.position: The document argues the restriction was based on limited early experience and that subsequent understanding of ARIA-E has reframed its management, noting the full 10 mg/kg biweekly dose is now used in ApoE4 carriers in the open-label extension and Clarity AD.
disagreements.attributed_to: The study authors (Eisai Inc. and co-authors of this article), in contrast to the regulatory authority that imposed the restriction
disagreements.quote: The assessment of early ARIA-E cases that led to Study 201 design changes were determined based on limited experience and understanding of lecanemab at the time of trial initiation. Additional experience since that time, both with lecanemab and other anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies, has reframed the understanding and management of ARIA-E.

disagreements.question: What explains the increased brain volume loss observed on lecanemab treatment?
disagreements.position: The document states the volumetric MRI findings are consistent with reports for other amyloid-targeting agents, that the reasons are unclear, and that the long-term implications are unknown.
disagreements.attributed_to: The study authors of this article
disagreements.quote: While these effects are generally consistent with literature reports for other amyloid-targeting agents [–], the reasons for these observations are unclear, but may be related to antibody profile and Aβ clearance, as has been suggested previously [].

disagreements.question: Why did this trial detect clinical differences where most other disease-modifying agents did not?
disagreements.position: The document attributes it to confirmed amyloid pathology in all subjects, lecanemab's selectivity for soluble aggregated Aβ, the Bayesian adaptive design and use of ADCOMS.
disagreements.attributed_to: The study authors of this article
disagreements.quote: Most previously published studies using other putative disease-modifying agents for AD did not show appreciable clinical efficacy in phase 3 [, ]. In this study, it is considered that several features helped to optimize the detection of clinical differences in a relatively slowly progressing early Alzheimer’s disease population.
